FINAL IVX 100% COMPLETION — EXECUTE END TO END, DO NOT RETURN ANOTHER PARTIAL NARRATIVE

The current final verdict is PARTIAL.

Do not create another report that only describes the blockers.
Execute the work necessary to close every blocker and return verifiable production evidence.

OBJECTIVE

Move the project from:

FINAL VERDICT: PARTIAL

to:

FINAL VERDICT: VERIFIED 100%

Repository:
ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform

Production backend:
https://api.ivxholding.com

Current production commit reported:
3b14ccb4d1ce869e700ea1d905084d859f5bf392

Current local HEAD reported:
c94f6dbe

==================================================
PHASE 1 — RECONCILE LOCAL, GITHUB, AND PRODUCTION
==================================================

The local branch is approximately 10 commits ahead of GitHub and is not identical to production.

1. Freeze changes temporarily.
2. Fetch the remote repository.
3. Confirm the exact current branch.
4. Show:
   - git status
   - git branch --show-current
   - git log --oneline -15
   - git rev-parse HEAD
   - git rev-parse origin/main
   - git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD
5. Review all local-only commits.
6. Confirm that none contain:
   - secrets
   - test-only shortcuts
   - fake data
   - Rork runtime dependencies
   - broken environment assumptions
   - destructive migrations
7. Run the full test suite before pushing.
8. Push the approved local commits to the owner-controlled GitHub repository.
9. Do not force-push unless absolutely required.
10. Do not discard the local commits.
11. Trigger the Render production deployment from the final GitHub commit.
12. Wait for deployment completion.
13. Verify all three SHAs are identical:

   LOCAL_HEAD
   GITHUB_HEAD
   PRODUCTION_COMMIT

Required result:

LOCAL_HEAD = GITHUB_HEAD = PRODUCTION_COMMIT

Do not mark this phase complete with only a short SHA. Return the full 40-character SHA.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — VERIFY RENDER DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

After the final GitHub push:

1. Confirm Render is connected to:
   - correct owner repository
   - correct branch
   - correct root directory
   - correct build command
   - correct start command
2. Confirm Render is not deploying an old repository or old branch.
3. Trigger one clean production deployment.
4. Return:
   - Render service name
   - Render deployment ID
   - deployment status
   - deployment start time
   - deployment finish time
   - full deployed commit SHA
   - production URL
5. Verify:
   - GET /health returns HTTP 200
   - GET /version returns HTTP 200
   - /health commit equals GitHub HEAD
   - /version commit equals GitHub HEAD
   - boot time is from the new deployment
6. Confirm no failed deployment is still marked as the latest production deployment.

Required result:

RENDER_STATUS: LIVE
SHA_MATCH: TRUE
HEALTH: 200
VERSION: 200

==================================================
PHASE 3 — ANDROID REAL-DEVICE QA
==================================================

The APK being structurally valid is not sufficient.

Install and test the release APK on a real Android device or a properly configured cloud Android device.

1. Produce a signed release APK.
2. Return:
   - exact APK filename
   - exact artifact path
   - file size
   - SHA-256
   - Android version tested
   - device manufacturer and model
   - application version
   - build number
   - package ID
3. Install the exact APK being reported.
4. Confirm a clean installation.
5. Confirm an upgrade installation over the previous IVX version.
6. Test the following flows on the installed APK:

Authentication:
- owner email/password sign-in
- invalid owner password rejection
- logout
- login again
- application restart with session persistence
- expired session handling
- password recovery
- non-owner access rejection
- fake-token rejection

Owner access:
- Owner Dashboard
- Admin Hub
- Variables
- Settings
- Members
- Investors
- Buyers
- JV Deals
- Tokenized
- Properties
- Reels
- Autonomous Dashboard
- IVX IA Chat

Registration:
- investor registration
- buyer registration
- JV deal registration
- tokenized member registration
- required email validation
- required cell validation
- duplicate registration handling
- member record created in Supabase
- new member visible in Members module

Stability:
- cold launch
- warm launch
- foreground/background recovery
- keyboard behavior
- navigation back/forward behavior
- no infinite loading
- no duplicated records
- no white screen
- no crash during reels playback
- no crash after repeated navigation
- no old cached code displayed

Media:
- image upload
- video upload
- reel playback
- PDF upload
- failed upload recovery

5. Capture screenshots and timestamped logs for every critical flow.
6. Confirm that the APK tested is byte-for-byte the APK delivered.

Required result:

ANDROID_INSTALL: PASS
ANDROID_CRITICAL_FLOWS: PASS
ANDROID_CRASHES: 0
ANDROID_BLOCKERS: 0

If Rork cannot access a physical Android device directly, use a supported cloud device-testing service. “No emulator in the sandbox” is not an acceptable final production result.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — IOS BUILD AND DEVICE QA
==================================================

“No macOS/Xcode in the Linux sandbox” is not a completed iOS result.

Use EAS Build, a macOS CI runner, or another legitimate Apple build environment.

1. Confirm:
   - Apple bundle identifier
   - Expo/EAS project
   - Apple signing credentials
   - provisioning profile
   - distribution certificate
2. Build the iOS production application.
3. Return:
   - EAS build ID
   - build URL
   - build status
   - application version
   - build number
   - bundle identifier
   - full Git commit SHA used
4. Install through TestFlight, internal distribution, or an approved development device.
5. Run the same critical authentication, owner access, registration, chat, reels, media, and stability tests used on Android.
6. Capture screenshots and timestamped evidence.

Required result:

IOS_BUILD: PASS
IOS_INSTALL: PASS
IOS_CRITICAL_FLOWS: PASS
IOS_CRASHES: 0
IOS_BLOCKERS: 0

Do not classify iOS as complete from source-code inspection only.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — CREDENTIAL RESOLUTION
==================================================

The report lists:

1. SUPABASE_DB_URL
2. STRIPE_API_KEY
3. IVX_GITHUB_READONLY_TOKEN

Handle each credential according to the actual feature requirement.

SUPABASE_DB_URL:
- Confirm whether the production system intentionally uses only the Supabase REST API.
- If direct SQL is not required, formally classify this variable as NOT REQUIRED.
- Remove it from the production blocker count.
- Document the architectural decision.
- Do not create a database URL unnecessarily.
- If migrations, direct SQL, or database-level health checks require it, configure it securely on Render and verify it without exposing the value.

STRIPE_API_KEY:
- If production payments are being launched now, configure the correct production Stripe secret key securely on Render.
- Confirm the key is server-only.
- Confirm no secret is in Expo public variables or the repository.
- Test one safe Stripe production-readiness flow without creating an unauthorized live charge.
- If payments are not launching in this release, formally set:
  PAYMENT_FEATURE_STATUS: DISABLED
  STRIPE_API_KEY_STATUS: NOT REQUIRED FOR CURRENT RELEASE
- Do not call it “missing” while simultaneously calling it optional.

IVX_GITHUB_READONLY_TOKEN:
- Configure a least-privilege read-only GitHub token if the autonomous audit system requires GitHub repository scanning.
- Scope it only to the required repository and read-only permissions.
- Confirm the token is stored server-side.
- Test the exact API request used by the audit scanner.
- Return only:
  token configured: yes/no
  permission check: pass/fail
  repository access: pass/fail
- Never display the token.

Credential final classification must use only:

VERIFIED
NOT REQUIRED
BLOCKED

Required result:

No credential may remain ambiguously labeled “optional but not configured.”

==================================================
PHASE 6 — AUTONOMOUS SYSTEM LIVE VERIFICATION
==================================================

The previous report states that 33 autonomous runs exist, but a fresh run could not be triggered from the sandbox.

Complete one new production run after the final deployment.

1. Trigger one QA-only autonomous job from the production control plane.
2. Use owner authentication.
3. Use the required single-use approval gate.
4. Confirm:
   - job created
   - job queued
   - job started
   - job heartbeat active
   - logs streamed
   - job completed
   - evidence stored
   - approval consumed only once
5. Confirm that retrying the consumed approval fails safely.
6. Confirm no unauthorized mutation is allowed.
7. Return:
   - job ID
   - run ID
   - creation timestamp
   - start timestamp
   - completion timestamp
   - final status
   - production commit SHA
   - evidence record ID
8. Confirm the run appears in the Autonomous Dashboard and IVX IA Chat report.

Required result:

FRESH_AUTONOMOUS_RUN: PASS
SINGLE_USE_APPROVAL: PASS
PROOF_LEDGER: PASS
UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS: REJECTED

==================================================
PHASE 7 — DATABASE TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION
==================================================

Do not declare data complete based only on page counts.

Audit the real production database.

Verify and return exact counts for:

- members
- investors
- buyers
- properties
- deals
- reels
- messages
- media
- documents
- transactions
- lenders
- revenue
- wallet
- jv_deals
- holdings
- landing_submissions
- landing_deals
- conversations
- conversation_participants
- chat_rooms
- room_messages
- ivx_owner_ai_messages
- ivx_owner_ai_conversations

For every table:

1. Count total rows.
2. Count active rows where applicable.
3. Count duplicates using the correct natural keys.
4. Count orphan references.
5. Count null required fields.
6. Identify test/demo/fake records.
7. Identify source provenance.
8. Confirm row-level security.
9. Confirm owner access.
10. Confirm non-owner restrictions.

Specific concerns:

- Verify whether the three deals are real production deals or owner test records.
- Verify that the 1,817 investor count is not duplicate pagination or seeded data.
- Verify buyer provenance.
- Do not describe SEC EDGAR sourced leads as verified investors unless they have completed IVX registration or qualification.
- Separate:
  public lead
  sourced prospect
  registered member
  verified investor
  qualified buyer
  active deal participant

Required result:

DATABASE_RECONCILIATION: PASS
DUPLICATES: 0 unresolved
ORPHANS: 0 unresolved
FAKE_PRODUCTION_DATA: 0
UNKNOWN_PROVENANCE: 0 unresolved

==================================================
PHASE 8 — SECURITY FINALIZATION
==================================================

Re-run security testing after the final deployment.

Verify:

- owner endpoints reject missing tokens
- owner endpoints reject malformed tokens
- owner endpoints reject expired tokens
- owner endpoints reject non-owner users
- owner endpoints reject fake JWTs
- secrets are never returned in HTTP responses
- service-role key remains server-only
- rate limiting is active
- audit events are persisted
- deployment actions require owner confirmation
- GitHub write actions require owner confirmation
- Render deployment requires owner confirmation
- single-use approvals cannot be replayed
- registration endpoints have abuse protection
- file uploads validate type and size
- SQL injection tests pass
- XSS tests pass
- path traversal tests pass
- CORS is restricted correctly
- production logs do not expose secrets
- no Rork runtime dependency remains

Required result:

SECURITY_TESTS: PASS
CRITICAL_VULNERABILITIES: 0
HIGH_VULNERABILITIES: 0
EXPOSED_SECRETS: 0

==================================================
PHASE 9 — FINAL CROSS-PLATFORM PARITY
==================================================

Confirm Android, iOS, and web use:

- the same production backend
- the same Supabase project
- the same authorization rules
- the same production data
- the same role definitions
- the same owner-access rules
- the same module naming
- the same application version strategy

Verify that none of the platforms uses:

- local fake data
- a separate local database
- an old API URL
- an old Render service
- an old Supabase project
- stale embedded credentials
- deprecated routes
- a Rork API or runtime dependency

Required result:

WEB_ANDROID_IOS_PARITY: PASS

==================================================
PHASE 10 — FINAL ACCEPTANCE TABLE
==================================================

Return a final table containing at least:

1. Local/GitHub/production SHA parity
2. GitHub push completed
3. Render deployment live
4. /health verified
5. /version verified
6. Android APK generated
7. Android APK installed
8. Android critical flows
9. Android stability
10. iOS build generated

25. Media uploads
26. IVX IA Chat

29. Single-use owner approval

36. No critical blockers
37. Web/Android/iOS parity

40. Final owner handoff

Allowed status values:

PASS
FAIL
BLOCKED
NOT REQUIRED

Do not use PARTIAL for the final response.

==================================================

==================================================

Return exactly:

FINAL RESULT

OWNER ACTION REQUIRED

FINAL VERDICT RULE

You may state:

only when:

Otherwise state:

and identify the exact external dependency, responsible party, and required action.

EXECUTE NOW.
DO NOT RETURN ANOTHER PLANNING REPORT.
DO NOT LABEL STRUCTURAL INSPECTION AS DEVICE QA.
DO NOT MARK OPTIONAL CREDENTIALS AS PRODUCTION BLOCKERS WITHOUT A FEATURE REQUIREMENT.
DO NOT CLAIM 100% WITHOUT REAL ANDROID AND IOS INSTALLATION EVIDENCE.
